distanceAime.q1: What do your calls look like now, compared with the start?
distanceAime.q1a: They've almost disappeared, we barely text.
distanceAime.q1c: Less frequent than at the start, but we take our time when we do call.
distanceAime.q1d: As regular as before, and sometimes we go on for hours.
distanceAime.q2a: Always me, and sometimes with no reply.
distanceAime.q2c: A bit of both, without keeping score.
distanceAime.q2d: As much one as the other, and sometimes we text at the same moment.
distanceAime.q3: What do you talk about when you talk?
distanceAime.q3a: Nothing, we swap "you okay?" and that's the end of it.
distanceAime.q3c: Our days, with real conversations from time to time.
distanceAime.q3d: Everything, including what isn't going well, as if we lived in the same place.
distanceAime.q4: And the next visit, how does it get organised?
distanceAime.q4a: There's no date any more, and the subject has become uncomfortable.
distanceAime.q4b: We talk about it vaguely, without ever booking anything.
distanceAime.q4c: A date is set, even if it sometimes moves.
distanceAime.q4d: The next one is locked in, and we're already talking about the one after.
distanceAime.q5: What place do you have in their life over there?
distanceAime.q5a: I know almost nobody, and nobody seems to know me.
distanceAime.q5b: Their close circle knows I exist, nothing more.
distanceAime.q5c: I've been introduced to their friends, on video or in person.
distanceAime.q5d: I'm part of their daily conversations with the people around them.
distanceAime.q6: When you ask who they spent the evening with?
distanceAime.q6a: The answer is vague, or the question annoys them.
distanceAime.q6b: I get an answer, but I have to push.
distanceAime.q6c: They answer plainly, without me having to ask twice.
distanceAime.q6d: They tell me about the evening before I even ask.
distanceAime.q7: Do you still get attentions that serve no purpose?
distanceAime.q7a: Not at all, that stopped a long time ago.
distanceAime.q7b: Very rarely, and usually to make up for something.
distanceAime.q7c: Yes, now and then, a message or a photo for no reason.
distanceAime.q7d: Often, and sometimes things that took planning ahead.
distanceAime.q8: Where are you on ending the distance?
distanceAime.q8a: We don't talk about it any more, and I've stopped asking.
distanceAime.q8b: We talk about it, but nothing ever gets decided.
distanceAime.q8c: There's a plan, with a rough deadline.
distanceAime.q8d: There's a date, or at least steps already under way.
distanceAime.q9a: It has completely gone, and nobody mentions it.
distanceAime.q9b: It has become rare and a bit mechanical.
distanceAime.q9c: It's still there, with ups and downs.
distanceAime.q9d: It's very much alive, and sometimes more inventive than before.
distanceAime.q10: What happens when a visit gets cancelled?
distanceAime.q10a: It happens often, and it doesn't seem to bother them.
distanceAime.q10b: It happens, and we don't always reschedule.
distanceAime.q10c: It's rare, and we find another slot straight away.
distanceAime.q10d: Almost never, and when it does they warn me well in advance.
distanceAime.q11: How is your relationship presented to others over there?
distanceAime.q11a: I don't know whether people even know we're together.
distanceAime.q11c: I'm spoken about as someone who matters.
distanceAime.q11d: I'm introduced as the partner, with no hesitation.
distanceAime.q12: What are the first hours of a reunion like?
distanceAime.q12a: Tense, it takes days to really find each other again.
distanceAime.q12b: There's a fairly long adjustment period.
distanceAime.q12c: A slight wobble, then everything comes back.
distanceAime.q12d: We pick up exactly where we left off.
distanceAime.q13: Are there silences you can't explain?
distanceAime.q13a: Yes, whole days with no news, regularly.
distanceAime.q13b: Yes, a few hours that turn strange, fairly often.
distanceAime.q13c: Rarely, and there's always a simple reason.
distanceAime.q13d: No, and when it happens I'm warned beforehand.
distanceAime.q14: When you bring up the future, how does it land?
distanceAime.q14a: The conversation gets dodged every time.
distanceAime.q14b: I get an answer, but it stays vague and ends quickly.
distanceAime.q14c: We talk about it seriously, without always concluding.
distanceAime.q14d: It's a normal subject, brought up by them too.
distanceAime.q15: And you, what brought you here?
distanceAime.q15a: I've felt alone in this relationship for a while.
distanceAime.q15b: Something has cooled and I can't put a name on it.
distanceAime.q15c: A passing doubt, in a stretch where we barely see each other.
distanceAime.r1_t: The bond has stretched thin, and distance isn't the only cause
distanceAime.r1_d: What you describe goes beyond the fatigue of a long-distance relationship: the calls have emptied out, the plans have gone, and the effort no longer looks shared. Distance makes everything harder, but on its own it doesn't explain someone ceasing to initiate, to tell you things and to plan ahead.
distanceAime.r1_a: The question is no longer "can we hold on" but "do we still want to". It deserves to be asked directly, at a calm moment, and an evasive answer will already be an answer. You deserve to know rather than to guess.
distanceAime.r2_t: There's still attachment, but distance is winning
distanceAime.r2_d: The feelings are probably still there. What has collapsed is the upkeep of the bond: fewer calls, fewer plans, less spontaneous news. It's the most common scenario in long-distance couples, and also the most reversible, provided you deal with it now rather than in six months.
distanceAime.r2_a: What puts distant couples back on track comes down to two very concrete things: a reunion date written in a diary, and a regular call that doesn't depend on the mood of the day. The rest almost always follows.
distanceAime.r3_t: The bond holds, it simply needs upkeep
distanceAime.r3_d: The essentials are there: they answer you, they tell you things, they picture you in what comes next. The weak points you describe are those of nearly every long-distance couple, and they have more to do with mismatched rhythms than with falling out of love.
distanceAime.r3_a: Watch out for a classic trap: at a distance, you end up talking only about logistics and good news, so as not to spoil the rare moments of contact. The couples who last are the ones who keep saying what isn't working, even over the phone.
distanceAime.r4_t: Yes, and it shows in nearly all your answers
distanceAime.r4_d: Balanced contact, conversations that go deep, an assumed place in the other's social life, a plan for ending the distance and reunions that pick up where you left off. That's the profile of a relationship that works, and distance doesn't change much about it.
distanceAime.r4_a: The only real risk at your stage is the wear of duration. The distant couples who hold up best are the ones who know how long it will last. If the deadline is still vague, that's the next subject to put on the table.
